He was Kinsman to <ns0:hi>Barnabas<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> Col.</ns0:hi> 4.10. it appears by that Text that he was at <ns0:hi>Rome</ns0:hi> with <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> and his fellow-labourer, <ns0:hi>Philemon</ns0:hi> 24.</ns0:note>, for he is profitable to me for the ministery <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">The Ministry of the Gospel. <ns0:hi>Pauls</ns0:hi> care was more for that, then for a ministring to himself, though he was a Prisoner.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="12">12 And <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Act. 20.4.</ns0:note> Tychicus have I sent to Ephesus <ns0:note n="u" place="bottom">I have given order to <ns0:hi>Tychicus,</ns0:hi> to come to <ns0:hi>Ephesus</ns0:hi> in thy absence.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="13">13 The cloke that I left at Troas with Car<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pus <ns0:note n="w" place="bottom">
                     <ns0:hi>Troas</ns0:hi> was a City in <ns0:hi>Asia,</ns0:hi> where we find <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> more then once, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 16.8. and 20.5 he preached Christ there, 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 2 12. there <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> left an upper garment with one <ns0:hi>Crispus,</ns0:hi> which probably (having no great Wardrobe) he might want, being a Prisoner.</ns0:note>, when thou comest, bring <ns0:hi>with thee x,</ns0:hi> and the books, <ns0:hi>but</ns0:hi> especially the parchments <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">Interpreters idly busie themselves in inquiring after what they can never find out, what these books were, or what was written in these parchments.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="14">14 Alexander the copper-smith did me much evil <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">We read of three <ns0:hi>Alexanders,</ns0:hi> one <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> 15.21. the Son of him that bare Christs cross, another <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 4.6. akin to <ns0:hi>Annas</ns0:hi> the <ns0:hi>High Priest</ns0:hi>; a third, <ns0:hi>Acts</ns0:hi> 19.33. probably the person here meant, for he was an <ns0:hi>Ephesian,</ns0:hi> but he at that time was a Disci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple of <ns0:hi>Pauls,</ns0:hi> as appears there, probably, afterward he Apo<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />statized, and was Excommunicated by <ns0:hi>Paul,</ns0:hi> 1 <ns0:hi>Tim.</ns0:hi> 1.20. which might possibly provoke him; what harm he did him, and where, whether at <ns0:hi>Ephesus</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>Rome,</ns0:hi> it is not said.</ns0:note>: the Lord reward him according to his works <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">How far it is lawful to pray against our enemies, (as <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> did here against <ns0:hi>Alexander</ns0:hi>) see the notes on <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 109.6. <ns0:hi>&c. Ier.</ns0:hi> 11.20. and 12.3. <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

                  </ns0:note> our words.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="16">16 At my first answer <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">At my first appearing before <ns0:hi>Nero,</ns0:hi> and the Court of <ns0:hi>Rome,</ns0:hi>

                     </ns0:gap> the Christians stood by me, or owned me;</ns0:note>, but all men forsook me <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">but all being frighted at my danger, left me alone to speak for my self.</ns0:note>: <ns0:hi>I pray God</ns0:hi> that it may not be laid to their charge <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">They sinned through weakness, and humane frailty, and the Lord I hope will pardon it, God grant them remission.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="17">17 Notwithstanding, the Lord stood with me <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">That is, did not leave me. It is opened by the next word,</ns0:note>, and strengthened me <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">he gave me courage and inward ability, so as I was able to plead, and to defend my cause.</ns0:note>, that by me the preaching might be fully known <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">That all men that heard me might fully know by Gods presence with me, seen in my cou<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rage, that my preaching was not from my self, or from men, but from God, the message of God by one to the sons of men.</ns0:note>, and <ns0:hi>that</ns0:hi> all the Gentiles might hear <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">And that al<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                        <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                     </ns0:gap> the Heathen present in the <ns0:hi>Court of Rome</ns0:hi> might hear and believe:</ns0:note>, and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lyon <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">And I was for the present delivered out of my great danger, or possibly he calls <ns0:hi>Nero</ns0:hi> (the <ns0:hi>Roman</ns0:hi> Empe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ror at that time) a <ns0:hi>Lyon</ns0:hi> for his barbarous cruelties.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="18">18 And the Lord shall deliver me from every evil work <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Faith riseth upon experience, 1 <ns0:hi>Sam.</ns0:hi> 17.37, 46. 2 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 1.10. By <ns0:hi>evil-work</ns0:hi> may be understood any sin into which <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> might fall through temptation: Or the <ns0:hi>evil works</ns0:hi> of others, designing mischief to the Apostle, he expresseth his faith in this term of various signification, to learn us how to exercise our Faith in God, in an evil time, <ns0:hi>viz.</ns0:hi> believing that God will ei<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther deliver us from our danger, or from sinning, by reason of our danger, for we have no foundation for our Faith, to be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lieve that God will at all times keep us from evils of suffering.</ns0:note>, and will preserve <ns0:hi>me</ns0:hi> unto his hea<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />venly kingdom <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">And that he will save us, and preserve us, if not as to a Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />poral Life, yet to a Coelestial, Honourable, Glorious Inheri<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tance.</ns0:note>, to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">This is an usual form of giving praise to God, desi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ring all honour might be given to him.</ns0:note>.</ns0:p>

               <ns0:p n="21">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:540" />21 Do thy diligence to come before winter <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">That is, to come to <ns0:hi>Rome</ns0:hi> to me before Winter, either be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause Sailing in the Winter time would be more dangerous, or because in the Winter time, he might have more need of his assistance.</ns0:note>, Eubulus greeteth thee, and Pudens, and Linus, and Claudia, and all the brethren <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">We have no further account of these persons in Holy Writ, the first is a <ns0:hi>Greek</ns0:hi> name, the rest <ns0:hi>Latin, Claudia</ns0:hi> is a womans name. <ns0:hi>Paul</ns0:hi> sends the respects of these persons, and all the other Christians that at that time were in <ns0:hi>Rome</ns0:hi> to <ns0:hi>Ti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mothy.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.</ns0:p>
